summary: The patched package (solution/fix.patch applied by solve.sh) implements every manual TD-7 rule within section-1 limits and keeps today's calculation, with today's constants, for the two items no rule reaches (the week a sub-2,000-cent correction counts toward, and the share paid on a partial-earnings week below 1,000 cents), as instruction.md paragraph 2 requires. I found no concrete incorrect behavior on any normal, boundary or interaction path.
checks_performed: Checked that fix.patch applies: hunk headers and context lines match the shipped disability.py, partial.py, payroll.py and rates.py line for line. Old and new line counts agree for every hunk. solve.sh runs `cd /; patch -p1`, which maps a/app/src/... to /app/src/..., and the Dockerfile installs patch. The driver is not touched.

Traced sample-job.json by hand through the patched logic (a static trace; nothing was executed). Injury on Wed 2025-03-12 puts the week of injury at Sun 03-16, so the base period is Sundays 2024-12-15..2025-03-09. Each week's-pay line counts toward F-5, so 13 of them land in the base period. The 37-cent correction counts toward its payday's week, 01-26, which is in the base period. Base wages are 1,389,428, so AWW = 106879. The first row is in force, so the rate is round(2/3*106879) = 71253. Disability days are 25+4 = 29, giving waiting 3, retro 3, paid 29, and ttd = 71253*29/7 = 295191. TPD is 43253+30253.

Checked week crediting: for a Friday payday F, week_ending(F)-7 = F-5, which is the Sunday whose following Friday is F (manual 2.2/3.1). Lines under 2,000 cents keep the payday's week, which is today's step because no manual rule places them (3.2).
Checked the AWW: base-period sum /13, rounded half up (3.3, 1.1). With no base wages the AWW is 0, which removes the shipped divide-by-zero on weeks_paid = 0.

Checked the rate: the row in force is the last row with from <= injury (2.4); a default of table[0] is never used, because 1.3 guarantees injury >= first row date. An AWW below the minimum returns the AWW itself (3.5). Otherwise the rate is round(2/3 AWW) clamped to [min, max] (3.4). Rounding before clamping is equivalent to clamping first, because the bounds are integers and rounding is monotone.

Checked disability: days are inclusive on both ends (2.5), the waiting period is min(3, days) (2.6), retro equals waiting when days >= 14 (4.1), paid = days - waiting + retro (4.2), and ttd = half_up(rate*paid, 7) (4.3, 1.1).

Checked partial: loss = AWW - earned or 0 (2.7). Weeks earning >= 1,000 cents get 2/3 of the loss, rounded and capped at the rate (2.8, 5.1). Lower weeks keep today's 3/5 share and rate cap, applied to the manual's AWW, loss and rate, per the paragraph-2 rule that unreached calculations keep today's steps and constants. tpd_weeks counts every week (6.1), and tpd is the sum (5.2).
Checked the statement: keys match the README order, every value except claim is an integer, the claim is passed through as given, and job order is kept.
Checked half-up rounding: the divisors 13, 3, 5 and 7 are odd, so no exact half ever arises and the tie-break cannot matter.
Checked model.py as a cross-reference only, not as an independent argument. Its rules agree with the patch on every branch listed above.

rules: 5.1 partial benefit capped at the rate
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: AWW below the minimum, with partial weeks: the rate is the AWW, and 2/3 of a loss is at most 2/3 AWW, which is below the cap. For low weeks, 3/5 of the loss is also below the AWW, so the cap is consistent.

rules: 2.2/3.1 week's pay credited to the prior week
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A payday in the week of injury pays the last base week, so it is included. A payday in the first base week pays the week before the base period, so it is excluded. A correction on either payday keeps the payday's week, per today's step.
Disability days of 1, 2, 3, 13 and 14 (including 14 spread over several periods): waiting = min(3, days), and retro is 3 only when days >= 14.
The minimum used by the 3.5 check and the 3.4 clamp both come from the row in force on the injury date, not the newest row.
The AWW is rounded before it is used in the rate and the wage loss. Each per-week benefit is rounded before the cap and the sum. TTD is rounded once, on rate*paid/7.
